title: Minimum Number of Lines to Cover Points
summary: Given an array of points on an X-Y plane, determine the least number of straight lines required to ensure each point is covered by at least one line.
statement: Given an array of points on an X-Y plane, determine the least number of straight lines required to ensure each point is covered by at least one line.
constraints: A line may cover any number of collinear points; every point must be covered.
Return the minimum number of infinite straight lines.
hints: A DP state is the set of already covered points; an optimal next line may be chosen through the first uncovered point.
Precompute the collinear mask for every point pair, then recurse on covered masks.
Try a singleton line and every pair line through first; memoize the minimum one plus the remaining state.
Any optimal cover has a line through the first uncovered point, represented by one of these choices, so the recurrence is exhaustive.
editorial: Any optimal cover has a line through the first uncovered point, represented by one of these choices, so the recurrence is exhaustive.

tests.explanation: The first three collinear points share one line and the remaining point needs a second.
All points lie on one line, so one line suffices.
